text:
Adam Edstrom spent parts of three seasons as a Rangers depth piece. In Nashville he is playing 15 minutes a night, up from 9:28 last season: six goals, 78 hits and 22 blocked shots through 17 games. At 6'7" he is also fast, with bursts of top speed in the 95th percentile.

The goals are not a fluke. His shooting percentage looks high, but his 5.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances, measured in goals) almost exactly match his six goals, because he scores from close in, like the tip against Carolina on November 3. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small six-game sample, has him on the end of 2.9 shots per 60 minutes off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the kind that go in most often.

Nashville also plays better with him out there: at five on five the Predators get 52% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 7 points better than without him. He rarely carries the puck into the zone, so his line lives on dump-ins and the forecheck. Our range still has him at 16 to 28 goals this season.
headline: Adam Edstrom has earned a real job in Nashville
